A strong non-oxidizing acid (like HCl) can react with metals that are more reactive than hydrogen in the reactivity series. These metals will displace hydrogen from the acid, forming a salt and hydrogen gas.

A. Aluminum and iron - Both are above hydrogen in the reactivity series. Aluminum reacts with strong acids to form aluminum salts and hydrogen gas. Iron reacts with strong acids to form iron salts and hydrogen gas.

B. Calcium and potassium - These are highly reactive metals (alkali and alkaline earth metals) that are well above hydrogen in the reactivity series. They would react vigorously with acids.

C. Gold and silver - These are noble metals that are below hydrogen in the reactivity series. They do not react with non-oxidizing acids.

D. Lead and tin - These metals are close to hydrogen in the reactivity series. Lead is generally below hydrogen and doesn't react with non-oxidizing acids. Tin is slightly above hydrogen and can react slowly with strong acids.
